thread.title: Global Weekly Charts Predict Worldwide Bear Market For Stocks

author: Richard Henry Suttmeier
title: Global Weekly Charts Predict Worldwide Bear Market For Stocks
text:
The weekly charts for all five major U.S. equity averages ended March and the first quarter of 2018 negative. The major averages in Japan, China, India and Germany are also negative. Traders can continue to trade if they buy on weakness to a value level and have the discipline to book profits on strength to a risky level or have a stop loss strategy.
Investors should use strength to risky levels to reduce holdings to the minimum allocations to global stock markets. 
All weekly charts are negative! 
All nine global averages ended March below their five-week modified moving averages with their 12x3x3 weekly slow stochastic readings declining between 80.00 and 20.00. This indicates risk to value levels and favors a strategy to sell strength to risky levels. This is a forecast that from the most recent all-time or multi-year highs the downside risk is at least 20% and the odds of trading 20% high are near zero percent. This does not mean we are headed for an April crash, but beware of the old axiom to ‘sell in May and go away.’ Here’s The First Quarter 2018 Scorecard 


Global Market Consultants Scorecard For Global Averages
  The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DIA) 
The Dow 30 is down 2.5% year-to-date and is 9.4% below its all-time intraday high of 26,616.71 set on Jan. 26. The eight ‘ Dogs of the Dow ’ are down an aggregate 7.5% year-to-date with Merck (MRK), Procter & Gamble (PG), Verizon (VZ) and ExxonMobil (XOM) setting 2018 lows in the last week of March. 10 of 30 Dow stocks set 2018 lows in the last week of March. 19 of 30 Dow stocks are in correction territory, and GE is deep into bear market territory. Should GE remain a Dow component? Daily Chart: This week’s value level is 23,652 with the 200-day simple moving average of 23,412 and my semiannual value level of 23,018. My quarterly and monthly risky levels are 25,280 and 26,133, respectively. Must Read: 8 Stocks To Sell For 2018 
The S&P 500 

The S&P 500 is down 1.2% year-to-date and is 8.1% below its all-time intraday high of 2,872.87 set on Jan. 26. Apple, Microsoft and Amazon.com are the three largest components. AAPL is performing with the S&P 500. MSFT is in correction territory and suffered a ‘key reversal’ day on March 13 after setting its all-time high of $97.24. AMZN is in correction territory but is still up 23.8% year-to-date. It too suffered a ‘key reversal’ day on March 13 after setting its all-time high of $1,617.54. Daily Chart: This week’s value level is 2,615.4 with the 200-day simple moving average of 2,589.19. Holding the 200-day simple moving average is one of the most important technical indicators. My annual, quarterly and monthly risky levels are tight at 2,769.1, 2,777.3 and 2,797.9, respectively. My semiannual pivot remains at 2,648.4. The Nasdaq Composite 
The Nasdaq is up 2.3% year-to-date and is 7.5% below its all-time intraday high of 7,637.27 set on March 13. The Nasdaq suffered a ‘key reversal’ day on March 13 as did so many tech stocks including semiconductor stocks. Daily Chart: My annual and semiannual pivots are 6,928 and 6,782, respectively, which both held on weakness. These are above the 200-day simple moving average of 6,742.34. My weekly, quarterly and monthly risky levels are 7,176, 7,381 and 7,483, respectively. The Dow Transportation Average 
The Dow Transports is down 2% year-to-date and is 9% below its all-time intraday high of 11,423.92 set on Jan. 16. Daily Chart: My weekly value level is 10,186 with the 200-day simple moving average of 9,994.06. My semiannual pivot is 10,435. My quarterly, monthly and annual risky levels are 10,858, 11,267 and 11,401, respectively. The Russell 2000 
The Russell 2000 is down 0.4% year-to-date and is 5.3% below its all-time intraday high of 1,615.52 set on Jan. 24. Daily Chart: My weekly pivot is 1,531.81 with the 200-day simple moving average of 1,487.79. My semiannual value level is 1,454.79 with my monthly risky level of 1,602.55. My annual and quarterly risky levels are 1,644.90 and 1,696.46, respectively. The Nikkei 225 
The Nikkei 225 is down 5.8% year-to-date and in correction territory, 11.1% below its multi-year intraday high of 24,129.34 set on Jan. 23. The Japanese benchmark set its 2018 low of 20,347.49 on March 26. Daily Chart: Has been trading back and forth around its 200-day simple moving average since Feb. 14 with this average now at 21,330. My semiannual and annual pivots are 21,961 and 22,009, respectively. The Shanghai Composite 
The Shanghai Composite is down 4.2% year-to-date and in correction territory, 11.7% below its multi-year intraday high of 3,587.03 set on Jan. 29. There is risk of a ‘death cross’ formation as early as this week. Daily Chart: Has been well below its 200-day simple moving average since March 14 with this average now at 3,313.27. The 50-day simple moving average is declining at 3,327.12. My annual value level is 2,475 with my semiannual risky level of 4,315. The Nifty 50 
The Nifty 50 is down 4% year-to-date and down 9.5% below its all-time intraday high of 11,171.55 set on Jan. 29. India’s benchmark set its 2018 low of 9,951.90 on March 23. Daily Chart: Ended the first quarter just below its 200-day simple moving average at 10,180.22. My annual pivot is 10,008 with my semiannual risky level of 11,310. The German DAX 
The German DAX is down 6.4% year-to-date and is in correction territory, 11% below its all-time intraday high of 13,596.89 set on Jan. 23. The German benchmark set its 2018 low of 11,726.62 on March 26. Daily Chart: Has been below its 200-day simple moving average since Feb. 5. A ‘death cross’ was confirmed on March 19 and now the 50-day simple moving average of 12,497 is well below the 200-day simple moving average of 12,682. My semiannual and annual risky levels are 12,814 and 13,563, respectively.  ---
